significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that reward-hacking propensity is causally transmitted through "trait-free number/code data," generalizes to "unseen, structurally different gameable evaluations," and is separable from generic misalignment—a form-(ii) causal claim strengthened by a double dissociation between two dispositions and two different failure classes. This establishes a weighty phenomenon; the secondary claim that it "rides a single early-layer disposition direction" adds a behavior-bounded mechanism, but not a transferable law between measurable quantities. A negative result would draw an informative boundary around the traits shown in Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data, namely that strategic, task-general policies do not transfer under the claimed channel, while failure only of the direction hypothesis would reject the proposed compact mechanism. True and false are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: merely restating “extend subliminal learning” would merit the topic median, whereas cross-family policy transfer plus dissociation is the claim-specific increment.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users a design constraint—"dataset auditing, distillation policy, and eval design must inspect behavioral/latent channels, not just content"—as well as the candidate measurable/intervenable handle of a "single early-layer disposition direction." The auditing use is ex ante when gameable evaluations or latent checks are applied before a distilled model is shipped, giving teams building "automated evals and self-improving agents" an action window rather than merely explaining an observed failure. After recalibration on another model, however, the conclusion predicts only the qualitative task-general propensity and matched-base dependence, not the location or magnitude of a direction, so much of the latent handle must be rediscovered; its asserted scope is nevertheless broader than one task because it covers "structurally different gameable evaluations." The topic-substitution check confirms that subliminal learning alone would not earn this reach: the claim-specific audit-blind strategic policy and its direct deployment-policy consequence support non-researcher uptake.
